# Certifier conformance statement

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit.
     Source: documentation/compliance/certifiers/<certifier>/forms/*.yaml
     Regenerate: cd trazo-back && poetry run python manage.py certifier_conformance -->

How Trazo lines up against each certifying agent's own Organic System Plan forms, question by question. Registered: CCOF, WSDA.
Generated from the conformance register, which is checked against the shipped OSP module
registry by `certifications/tests/test_certifier_conformance_register.py` — a question that is
renamed, removed or added without a decision fails that test rather than quietly making
this document wrong.

Statuses: **Covered** — the fact is capturable and reaches an artifact a certifier reads.
**Partial** — captured but incomplete. **Not covered** — no home in the product today.
**Out of scope** — deliberately not built, with the reason stated.

Severity is about what a reviewer at that certifier does with it: **P0** the packet is bounced or
asserts something untrue · **P1** a request for information · **P2** noticed, tolerated ·
**P3** cosmetic.

### F Weed Management

*AGR 2121 · R 02/25 · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** Crop Producer Organic System Plan (AGR 2121) — filed by every crop producer applicant applying for or renewing WSDA organic certification

**7 items** — Partial 3 · Not covered 4

> This form's register entry is a draft — treat absences as unreviewed, not as gaps.

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which monitoring practices do you implement to determine the effectiveness of your weed management plan? (Comparison of crop yields / Observation of crop health / Observation of weeds / Other.) | Not covered | P1 | — | No structured field captures which METHOD is used to monitor weed-management effectiveness. The nearest Trazo fields — `g5_0_pest.monitoring_scope` (WHAT is monitored: pest/disease/weed/beneficial-activity categories) and `g5_0_pest.monitoring_records` (HOW results are recorded) — answer different questions than WSDA's METHOD ask, and neither can be cited as this row's answer: both are already registered in the CCOF side of this register as having no CCOF counterpart (CCOF's G5.0 has no monitoring section at all), and citing them here as 'this is where the answer lives' would contradict that entry rather than agree with it. This is a genuine WSDA-specific gap that CCOF's silence on monitoring had been masking. **Fix:** Add a `weed_monitoring_method` [checkbox_group] {crop_yield_comparison, crop_health_observation, weed_observation, other}, separate from the existing category/records fields. |
| 2 | How often do you make these comparisons or observations? | Not covered | P2 | — | Open-ended frequency question with no structured field. `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` is the adjacent existing field but, like `monitoring_scope`/`monitoring_records` above, is already registered as having no CCOF counterpart and cannot be cited here without contradicting that entry. **Fix:** Add a `weed_monitoring_frequency` field paired with the fix proposed at ref 1, or generalize `monitoring_frequency` to serve F/G/H's monitoring questions if the CCOF-side unmapped entry is ever revisited. |
| 3 | Which preventive weed control strategies do you implement on your operation? (Cover crop - Annual / Crop rotation / Crop spacing / Field preparation / Flame weeding / Hand weeding / Mechanical cultivation / Mowing / Natural mulch / Stale seed bed / Other.) | Partial | P1 | `g5_0_pest.weed_management_practices` · `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices` | CCOF asks these same practices inside ONE matrix (G5.0 §A, 23 practices × 4 pest-type columns: Weeds / Insects & invertebrates / Diseases & nematodes / Vertebrate pests), already registered `partial`/P1 there because Trazo's `prevention_practices` and `weed_management_practices` carry no pest-type dimension. WSDA makes the same underlying fact harder to answer cleanly, not easier: it splits pest management into three physically separate sections (this form, plus G Pest and H Disease), each expecting its own self-contained answer, instead of one table where a practice repeated across pest-type columns reads as normal. Half of WSDA's F3 list — crop rotation, crop spacing — lives in Trazo's generic, pest-type-blind `prevention_practices`, which a WSDA reviewer would see printed IDENTICALLY under the G and H sections too; in a matrix that reads as intentional (one row, several checked columns), across three independent PDF sections it reads as a copy-pasted answer that never differentiates weed-specific reasoning from disease-specific reasoning. The rest of the list (mechanical cultivation, hand weeding, mowing, natural mulch, flame weeding) does live in the weed-specific `weed_management_practices`, the right shape for this section — but even there, `crop_spacing`, `field_preparation` and `stale_seed_bed` have no matching option. On balance this does not rise to a bounced packet: the substantive content is present and responsive to the question asked. But it is more likely to draw an actual reviewer comment than CCOF's version of the same gap, because WSDA's layout puts the duplication in plain sight across three section headers instead of inside one table's columns, so this stays a P1 (request for information) rather than escalating. **Fix:** Same structural fix as CCOF's G5.0 §A: add a pest-type dimension to `prevention_practices` (matrix kind, or interim `pest_classes_addressed` checkbox group) so the compiled narrative can print a weed-specific paragraph for this section, a distinct one for G, and a distinct one for H instead of the same list three times. Also add `crop_spacing`, `field_preparation` and `stale_seed_bed` to `weed_management_practices`. |
| 4 | Do you use plastic mulch or silage tarps for weed control in an annual cropping system? 4a. If yes, describe how you ensure it is removed from the field at the end of the growing or harvest season. | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_used` · `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_removal` | Use and season-end removal are captured. Missing is the § 205.601(b)(2)(ii)-(iii) non-PVC material condition CCOF's own G5.0 §A register row already flags as absent from these same two fields. **Fix:** Same fix already proposed on the CCOF side: add `plastic_mulch_non_pvc` [radio] {confirmed_non_pvc, biobased_film, unknown}, visible when `plastic_mulch_used`. |
| 5 | Do you use plastic mulch or silage tarps for weed control in a perennial cropping system? 5a. If yes, describe how you ensure the plastic remains in sufficient condition that prevents decomposition into the soil. | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_used` · `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_removal` | `plastic_mulch_removal` is framed around season-end removal in an annual system ('describe how the plastic or synthetic mulch is removed at season end'); it does not ask WSDA's actual perennial-system question — how the operation ensures the plastic stays intact enough to avoid decomposing into the soil over a multi-year planting. A perennial-crop operator answering this field today is describing the wrong practice. **Fix:** Add `plastic_mulch_perennial_condition` [textarea], visible when the operation's cropping system includes `perennial` (per `g4_0_rotation_soil.system_type`), separate from the annual-system removal question. |
| 6 | Describe the records you maintain regarding your preventative weed management strategies. | Not covered | P2 | — | No field captures what records are kept for preventative weed-management practices specifically. `monitoring_records` (§ 205.201(a)(3)) is the nearest existing field but answers a different question (how MONITORING results are recorded, not what records document the preventative practices themselves), and — like the fields discussed at ref 1 — is already registered as having no CCOF counterpart, so it is not cited here as this row's answer. **Fix:** Add `weed_prevention_records` [textarea] describing what preventative-practice records are kept. |
| 7 | Optional space for additional information. | Not covered | P3 | — | No general free-text notes field exists on the pest-management module for information outside the structured questions above — the same class of gap CCOF's G4.2 A9 already names for its own module. **Fix:** Add an optional `weed_management_additional_notes` textarea. |

Additionally add `trap_crops` (per CCOF's own register), `companion_planting`, `mating_disruption` and `insect_rodent_traps` as options. |
| 5 | Describe the records you maintain regarding your preventative pest management efforts. | Not covered | P2 | — | Same gap as F6: no field captures what records document the preventative practices themselves, as distinct from monitoring-result records (`monitoring_records`, already registered as having no CCOF counterpart). **Fix:** Add `pest_prevention_records` [textarea]. |

Two of CCOF's options require an attachment ('written agreement with neighbor', 'written agreement with the roadside agency'), but G6.0 declares no upload question at all, and even where module uploads exist elsewhere in the OSP they are tagged to the DMS by module only — `generate_osp_packet` ships only the `receipts/` folder, so an attached agreement would still never reach the packet. 'Residue testing' (`residue_testing`) is worded as incident-driven, not CCOF's routine monitoring testing. `drift_response_procedure` is a Trazo-only superset question (§ 205.400(f)(1), answering the form's opening instruction to notify CCOF immediately of drift) rather than one of the ten checkboxes. **Fix:** Add an exclusive `none_no_surrounding_prohibited_use` option; add `drift_agreements_upload` [upload, opt] and wire `generate_osp_packet` to pull module uploads (tagged by `linked_section`) into `attachments/<module>/`, not just `receipts/`; add `drift_registry_name` [text]; split `roadside_utility_registration` into a registration option and a `roadside_agency_agreement` option (+ upload); relabel `self_managed_adjacent` and add a `self_managed_precautions` textarea; add `residue_testing_routine`. |

Nonretail containers (any container used to ship or store organic product that is not for retail sale, including temporary signage) must identify the product as organic — unless the container holds retail-packaged product with organic status visible through it — and must display a production lot number, shipping identification, or other unique identifier linking to your audit trail. Do you use any nonretail containers (produce boxes, bins, totes, bags, etc.) for shipping or storage of organic crops? If yes, attach all nonretail container labels and provide color samples if the USDA seal is used. | Partial | P1 | `g7_0_labeling.product_leaves_as` · `g7_0_labeling.label_claim_review_process` · `g7_0_labeling.label_files_upload` | The `unlabeled_bulk_documents` option and the module's NA state let an operation attest that organic identity lives only on invoices/BOL, a state CCOF's own container-identification rule treats as non-compliant (§ 205.307(a)(1) requires the container or temporary signage itself to identify the product as organic) — with no write-time notice. `label_claim_review_process` asks who reviews labels but not whether each label was actually sent to or approved by the certifier. | F | Table, by National List material type — Ammonium carbonate, Boric acid, Botanical pesticides, Carbon dioxide, Diatomaceous earth, Nitrogen gas, Nonsynthetic bait/lure/repellent, Pheromones, Pyrethrum/pyrethrins, Sticky traps, Vitamin D3 — each with Used?, Where Used, and Applied by fumigation/fogging? (Yes/No). Or 'Not applicable.' | Not covered | P1 | `g9_0_facility_pest.material_tier` · `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation` | G9.0 collapses all of this to a single `material_tier` radio (none / non-production-only / National List / synthetic-approved); there is no per-type row, no where-used field, and no fumigation/fogging flag anywhere for facility pest control. Only 5 of the 11 National List types are seeded as substances at all (ammonium carbonate, boric acid, sticky traps, pheromones, vitamin D3); the pilot answers `material_tier = none` with snap traps recorded only as a mechanical control. **Fix:** Replace or augment `material_tier` with a checkbox_group of the 11 National List types, each with `where_used` and `applied_by_fumigation`; seed the six missing substances; compile a table from the answers. |
| G | List any pest control material used in a post-harvest handling or crop-storage facility that does not fit a §F National List type (e.g., 'MAX Fog Roach Killer / Storage room / Yes'): Non-National List Material, Where Used, Applied by fumigation/fogging? Or 'Not applicable.' / 'Other list attached.' | Not covered | P1 | `g9_0_facility_pest.material_tier` | G9.0's `synthetic_approved` option promises materials 'approved by our certifier in advance and entered on our OSP inputs list' — but the registry cannot hold a non-National-List synthetic at all (no free-text row; `verify_input` would return a § 205.105 prohibited hit or nothing). G6.2's free-text description is the only place such a material can be named today. **Fix:** Add category G to the operator-authored row (name, where used, fumigation flag, certifier-approval reference); have G9.0's `synthetic_approved` path link to it instead of asserting an approval Trazo cannot record. |

The distinction is not pedantic: `not_covered` reads as "build this from scratch", while the real work is routing an existing table to a second artifact. **Fix:** Render the prior-controller table (owner/manager, name, start MM/YY, end MM/YY) in the Parcel Application §F instead of the bare affidavit count, reusing the dossier's existing table, and state the 'N/A, full three years' case from `date_began_managing`. |

No → skip to §G. A buffer row's `prohibited_use_last_date` describes the NEIGHBOR's land, not the operator's own excluded ground; `ChemicalEvent.site_id` (the CA PUR site ID) is per event with no parcel-level rollup. A California orchard with a conventional block filed under the same PUR site ID — exactly what this question is for — has no way to answer it. **Fix:** Add `prohibited_on_borders_since_dlpm` (boolean) and a detail textarea on §F, visible when not currently certified; reuse the §E map-upload path; add an optional `pur_site_id` Parcel column for California establishments, printed in §A. |

| A2b | If you produce compost containing manure (and/or compost tea made from it), which production method do you use? Not applicable / windrow — reaches 131-170°F for at least 15 days, turned at least 5 times / in-vessel or static aerated pile — reaches 131-170°F for at least 3 days (maintain compost production records) / my compost does not meet either requirement, so it is considered 'raw manure' (complete section B). | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_method` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_initial_cn_ratio` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_temp_and_days` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_turnings` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_temp_logs_kept` | Superset on the numbers actually asked (C:N ratio, temperature range, turning count, kept logs) for the two real thermophilic pathways. Three defects: `compost_method` lists `vermicompost` as one of its own options, a category error (vermicompost is CCOF's separate A2c question, not a thermophilic method) that forces the required temperature/day/turning questions onto a worm system never meant to answer them; there is no selectable 'does not meet either requirement, so it is raw manure' outcome that opens page B; and there is no N/A for compost containing no manure at all, so plant-only compost (unrestricted under § 205.203(c)(3)) is still forced through the required thermophilic questions. **Fix:** Remove `vermicompost` from `compost_method` and from the temperature/turning fields' `visible_when`; add a `compost_contains_manure` boolean gate; replace the implicit failure case with an explicit `does_not_meet` option that reveals page B. |

| B1 | Do you apply raw animal manure (including any compost, compost tea, or vermicompost containing manure that does not meet the section A production requirements), and/or do you have planned grazing of animals in your organic crop production areas? A sheep-grazed orchard — routine in WA/CA orchards and vineyards — tells G5.0 it grazes and tells G4.1 'none of these are used', so the compiled § 205.201(a) narrative states something false by omission. **Fix:** Add `Option("planned_grazing", …)` to `materials_applied` (or a standalone boolean) and widen page B's `visible_when` to `includes_any (raw_manure, planned_grazing)`; relabel the `none` option; prefill a suggestion from `GR` events. |
| B2 | How do you meet the following restriction on the use of raw manure, either applied or from planned grazing? Mark all that apply. Used for crops that are not for human consumption / incorporated at least 120 days before harvest of crops whose edible portions contact soil or soil particles / incorporated at least 90 days before harvest of crops whose edible portions do not contact soil or soil particles. | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_interval_rule` · `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_timing_detail` | CCOF says 'mark all that apply'; Trazo's `raw_manure_interval_rule` is a single-select radio, so a diversified farm with both root crops and tree or bush crops cannot state both rules truthfully. Separately, the packet's own crop classifier that decides which sub-cite to print (§ 205.203(c)(1)(i) vs (ii)) treats any crop as soil-contact by default and its keyword override list omits blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, kiwi and hops — so an operator who correctly answers 'no soil contact, 90 days' for blueberries still gets the packet printing the 120-day soil-contact citation and can be flagged for a classification mismatch despite answering correctly. **Fix:** Change `raw_manure_interval_rule` to a `checkbox_group`. Separately (outside this module), extend `_manure_interval_rule_for_crop`'s keyword list or set `has_soil_contact=False` for the elevated berry/cane/kiwi/hop crops in the seeder. |
| B3 | How do you ensure that manure does not contaminate wells, rivers or streams, lakes or ponds? | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_water_risk` | CCOF requires an answer here; Trazo's `raw_manure_water_risk` is `required=False`, so a complete module can leave it blank. It is also only reachable when `materials_applied` includes raw_manure, so it never appears for the planned-grazing case even though § 205.203(c) applies to both. **Fix:** Set `required=True`; widen `visible_when` to `includes_any (raw_manure, planned_grazing)` once the B1 grazing trigger exists; cite § 205.203(c) explicitly. |

### Site Update Information

*AGR 2516 · R 01/20 · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** File when the Crop Production Information on your Certified Operation Profile no longer matches your plan for the coming year — crop, variety or acreage changes, or reduced total site acreage.

**3 items** — Partial 1 · Not covered 2

> This form's register entry is a draft — treat absences as unreviewed, not as gaps.

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hdr | Indicate what changes need to be made for each site where the Crop Production Information on the Certified Operation Profile does not match your current plan for the coming year — crops/varieties, acreages, and whether total site acreage will be reduced. Alternatively, production or planting records may be submitted instead, provided they clearly indicate the site number and site name as identified on your certificate. | Partial | P1 | `certifications.models.OSPChangeNotification` · `certifications.models.OSPAnnualUpdate` | The packet already carries a superset mechanism — `OSPChangeNotification` (categories include `acreage_field_addition` and `field_removal`, both citing § 205.400(f)(2)) and `OSPAnnualUpdate`'s `additions`/`deletions` JSON — so the SUBSTANCE of a site update is capturable. But neither is structured by a WSDA-assigned SITE NUMBER, which is the specific cross-reference WSDA's own Certified Operation Profile needs to locate the record; `OSPChangeNotification.parcel` links to Trazo's own `Parcel` row, and the parcel module has no `wsda_site_number` field at all (same gap as AGR 2264 ref '6'). **Fix:** Add the `wsda_site_number` field proposed for AGR 2264 ref '6' to the parcel module, and print it beside the parcel name on any WSDA-bound change notification or annual-update page. |
| Table | Table: WSDA site no., WSDA site name, and a plain-language description of the change (e.g., 'total site acreage remains the same', '5 acres moved to conventional, organic acreage is now 15 acres'). | Not covered | P2 | `certifications.models.OSPChangeNotification.description` | `OSPChangeNotification.description` is free text and can hold the same plain-language change statement WSDA's own table wants, but without the `wsda_site_number` field (see 'Hdr'), the printed change-notification page cannot reproduce WSDA's own two leftmost columns — a reviewer matching this page against the Certified Operation Profile has to do it by parcel name alone. **Fix:** Same as 'Hdr': add `wsda_site_number`, and format the printed row as 'WSDA site no. / site name / description' when it is set. Once captured, Trazo's own production and crop-history records could also double as the 'alternative records' AGR 2516 says may be submitted instead of this form — they cannot today, for the same reason. |
| Acreage removed | If acreage is removed from organic production, include a map identifying the new boundaries and include details on why the acreage was removed (e.g., transferred to another grower, converted to conventional). | Not covered | P1 | — | AGR 2516 asks for a boundary map AND the reason acreage was removed — and only when acreage is removed, with the form itself accepting "production records, planting records, etc." in place of the map. Re-registered on 2026-08-28: the map half is conditional and substitutable, so it is not the map defect. The other half is an unconditional Trazo defect of its own — `OSPChangeNotification.supporting_document` is a real writable FileField with NO UI writer (the panel says so itself), it is never written into the packet ZIP, and `_change_notifications_pdf` never names it. There is no `removal_reason` field either: `description` carries an ADDITION example in both help text and placeholder. So landing the shared map service would close the map half and still leave a WSDA reviewer reading "5 acres moved to conventional" with no reason and nothing attached. **Fix:** Two moves, both independent of the map service: (1) give `OSPChangeNotification` an upload control and write `supporting_document` into the packet ZIP alongside `receipts/`, naming it in `_change_notifications_pdf`; (2) add a `removal_reason` prompt shown when the change reduces certified acreage, and stop illustrating `description` with an addition. |

## Forms Trazo does not register

CCOF's Guide routes by activity, so what is absent is as readable as what is present.
A **decision** is an answer; a **gap** is a debt, and names where it is triggered from.

### Gaps

| Form | Triggered from | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Co-Packer Application (NOPB26) | G7.0 C — packing into a brand owned by another company | Not built and not triggered: G7.0's `buyer_label` option has no follow-up and Trazo has no brand-owner record, so a farm that packs into a buyer's label cannot say so. Real for wholesale growers who pack under a packer's brand. |
| Exempt Handler Affidavit (NOPB107) | G6.1 A2/A3 (uncertified harvester or transporter); G6.2 A (uncertified storage); G6.5 A1 (uncertified supplier) | No representation anywhere — no exemption classification, no trigger asking whether an uncertified operator's role requires certification or an affidavit, no upload. One missing concept behind three CCOF forms. |

### Deliberately not built

| Form | Reason |
|---|---|
| W2.0 Wild Crop Harvesting (NOPB48) | Trazo ships an N/A-attestable stub module so a crop grower can record that wild-crop harvesting does not apply, which is what a crop-scope OSP needs. Full wild-crop content (designated area, 36-month history of the harvest site, sustainability of the harvest) is not built: the ICP is cultivated orchard and berry ground. |
| Handler / Processor OSP forms (H-series) (NOPB32) | Trazo covers simple on-farm post-harvest handling of a farm's own crop (CCOF G6.4). Complex handling, multi-ingredient products and third-party processing are a different certification scope and a different product. A farm needing the H-series files it with its certifier directly. |
| Livestock OSP forms (L-series) (Guide to Livestock Producer OSP Forms) | Crop scope only. Nothing in the data model represents animals, feed, origin of livestock or living conditions, and pretending otherwise on a form would be worse than the absence. |
| Retail Establishment forms (R-series) (R1.0–R5.0) | Retail and restaurant operations are not producers. Out of scope by definition. |
| OCal Cultivator and Handler forms (OCal C-series / OCal H-series) | OCal is California's comparable-to-organic standard for cannabis. Different crop, different statute, different market. |
| COR (Canada) Handler forms (COR H-series) | Canadian Organic Regime equivalence. Out of scope while the market is US crop producers. |
| Global Market Access Application; Mexico Compliance Program; NOP Import Certificate Request (GMA04 and related) | Export-programme enrolment and the certificates themselves are transactions between the operation and CCOF. Trazo captures the export and import questions the Common OSP asks (destination countries, certificate types, request-and-retain process, port integrity) inside G8.0 page C, which is the recordkeeping half — it does not file for the certificates. |
| Contracted Partner Program Application (Guide item 17) | An arrangement where a CCOF-certified customer manages the grower's certification. A grower in that programme has no OSP of their own to keep. |
| Handler OSP (2180, sections A-P) (AGR 2180) | Trazo covers simple on-farm post-harvest handling of a farm's own crop (WSDA Crop Producer OSP §K Storage, §L Post-Harvest). Complex handling, multi-ingredient products and third-party processing are a different certification scope and a different product — WSDA licenses this as a separate 17-lettered-section Handler OSP (product flow through equipment cleaning and sanitation). A farm needing the Handler OSP files it with WSDA Organic Program directly. Same reasoning as CCOF's Handler/Processor OSP forms (H-series, NOPB32) exclusion — the product scope decision is the same regardless of certifier. |
| Processed Product Application (AGR 2523) | Application to add a processed (multi-ingredient) product to a handler's certified scope. Same handler/processor certification scope excluded above — Trazo does not carry a farm into a handler-scope application. |
| Handled Product Application (AGR 2524) | Application to add a handled (single-ingredient, minimally processed) product to a handler's certified scope. Same handler/processor certification scope exclusion as AGR 2523. |
| Multi- and Single-Ingredient Processed Product Formulation (AGR 2178 / AGR 2179) | Ingredient-percentage formulation worksheets for a handler's processed-product recipe. Handler-side; a grower shipping raw or lightly-handled crop has no 'formulation' to declare. Same handler/processor scope exclusion. |
| Natural Flavor Questionnaire (AGR 2700) | Characterizes a purchased natural-flavor ingredient's own processing, for a handler's product formulation. Handler-side ingredient sourcing; same scope exclusion. |
| Non-Organic Ingredient Affidavit (AGR 2252) | Attests a specific nonorganic ingredient's use, below the 5% threshold, in a 'Made with Organic' multi-ingredient product. Handler-side product formulation, not something a crop grower selling raw or lightly-handled produce needs — distinct from CCOF's Exempt Handler Affidavit gap (an uncertified transporter/storage/supplier exemption, which IS a real grower-side trigger and remains unrepresented in Trazo). |
| Ingredient Commercial Availability (AGR 2251) | WSDA's handler-side commercial-availability worksheet for a nonorganic ingredient in a processed product — distinct from the grower-side seed/planting-stock commercial availability question `g3_0_seeds.ca_search_before_use` already answers. Handler scope; same exclusion. |

## What Trazo asks that the registered forms do not

Not gaps — questions the federal Common OSP or the regulation itself asks for, which a
certifier's own grower overlay leaves implicit. Stated per agent: a question one asks and
the other does not is the most informative row here.

### CCOF

| Question | Why it has no CCOF counterpart |
|---|---|
| `certification_contract.contract_scopes` | Maps to the Contract's cover-page guide selection ('Guide to Grower OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Handler OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Livestock Producer OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Retail Establishment OSP Forms') rather than to any of the Contract's own lettered/numbered questions (A-H); Trazo captures the choice as a structured field instead of a forms checklist. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_mitigation_practices`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_plan_upload` | Optional upload for a written fraud-prevention plan. CCOF's G8.0 D references an external 'Fraud Prevention Plan worksheet' as guidance and reserves the right to request one for complex operations, but the grower form itself does not ask for an attachment. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_risk_areas`; not a separate CCOF question — G8.0 D1 is a fixed checklist of scenarios with no open-ended 'other'. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_accuracy_process` | Who keeps the OSP accurate, and how. The Certification Contract B2 asks only review FREQUENCY (annually/quarterly/monthly/other); it does not ask who performs the review or how, which this question captures beyond what either form requests. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_implementation_monitoring_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `osp_implementation_monitoring`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.product_testing_detail` | Free-text elaboration (what is tested, and how often) for the `product_testing` option inside `fraud_mitigation_practices`; not asked as its own CCOF question. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.planting_stock_description` | CCOF's G3.0 has no general planting narrative question. This is the § 205.103 source-and- planting record (where the stock came from, where and when it was planted) Trazo captures for the invoice-to-block trace an inspector performs — beyond anything G3.0 itself asks. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.planting_stock_upload` | The attachment mechanism for `stock_records_kept` above; same reason — CCOF's G3.0 has no numbered question calling for a stock-paperwork upload. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_records_kept` | CCOF's B3 asks for commercial-availability search records specifically. This is Trazo's broader general recordkeeping battery for the stock itself (invoices, organic certificates, variety tags, phytosanitary certificates, planting map, treatment statements) — CCOF has no distinct numbered question for it beyond the generic inspection-records expectation in G8.0. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_treatments` | CCOF's G3.0 section D asks about SEED treatments only; it has no question about whether purchased planting stock itself was treated before or at delivery. Trazo superset for § 205.204 traceability. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_types_established` | CCOF's G3.0 asks only whether planting stock is organic or non-organic (A3); it never asks which propagation forms (bare-root, containerized, rootstock, cuttings/scions, crowns/divisions) were established. Trazo's own § 205.103 establishment-record granularity. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.suppliers_on_supplier_list` | CCOF's G3.0 never asks whether stock suppliers are entered on a Supplier List — that traceability expectation lives in Common OSP § 11 / G8.0 Record Keeping, not on the G3.0 form itself. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_documentation` | CCOF's G4.1 requires only that purchased compost/manure appear on the Grower Materials Application (OSP Materials List, section A1); it does not ask the operator to keep the supplier's process description or analysis on file. Trazo superset. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_upload` | The attachment mechanism for `purchased_compost_documentation` above; same reason. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_quality_test_frequency` | Companion frequency field to `water_quality_tested` above; same reason. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_quality_tested` | Trazo's own addition — feeds the `natural_resources_condition` record type — with no counterpart on either NOPB43 or NOPB40's section D. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` | § 205.201(a)(3) monitoring plan. CCOF's G5.0 (NOPB42) has no monitoring section — this is superset tracking of how often pest/disease/weed monitoring is performed, with suggestions derived from the median gap between logged scouting records. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_records` | § 205.201(a)(3) monitoring plan. CCOF's G5.0 (NOPB42) has no monitoring section — this is superset tracking of how monitoring results are recorded. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_scope` | § 205.201(a)(3) monitoring plan. CCOF's G5.0 (NOPB42) has no monitoring section — this is superset tracking of what is monitored (pest populations, disease pressure, weed pressure, beneficial activity), paired with monitoring_frequency and monitoring_records below. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.containers_reused_barrier` | Companion detail field to containers_reused_from_prohibited — same reasoning. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.containers_reused_from_prohibited` | §205.272(b)(2) prohibits reusing a container/bin/trailer that held a prohibited substance for organic product unless adequately cleaned. No CCOF grower form among G6.1/G6.2/G6.4/G6.5 asks this as its own distinct numbered question — it is folded into the general "packaging materials... free of prohibited substances" concept (G6.4 C, answered on G6.1 §B per that row's cross-citation). Trazo asks container reuse from a prior prohibited-substance contact as its own explicit gate. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.lot_identification_on_every_load` | §205.103(b)(2) traceability fact. CCOF's G6.1 form does not carry a distinct numbered checkbox for lot identification on every load — it is implied by the form's general instruction that "records must be sufficient to trace organic crops/products from production to sale or transport." Trazo tracks it as its own boolean, tying lot identity through transport as FSMA 204 KDE preparation (see also g6_2_storage.lot_identity_maintained). |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.transport_units_inspected_clean` | §205.272(a) contamination-prevention fact. CCOF's G6.1 form addresses this only as general framing text ("you must use management practices and physical barriers to prevent commingling... and to prevent contamination from contact with prohibited substances") and via the B1 equipment-cleaning table, not as a distinct numbered checkbox for transport units specifically. Trazo asks it as its own explicit gate under "C. Transport & lot identity." |
| `g6_2_storage.lot_identity_maintained` | §205.272 / §205.103(b)(2) traceability fact. CCOF's G6.2 form does not ask a distinct "does every stored lot keep its lot identity" checkbox anywhere in Sections A or B. Trazo asks it as its own boolean, tying lot identity through storage as FSMA 204 KDE preparation (see also g6_1_harvest_transport.lot_identification_on_every_load). |
| `g6_4_handling.commingling_controls` | §205.272(a) commingling-prevention fact. CCOF's G6.4 form is scoped to all-organic, single-operation handling where commingling with nonorganic product is defined out of scope by the form's own applicability gate ("this form does not apply if you are handling both organic and nonorganic products"). Trazo still asks it to cover the custom_handling_separation branch (handling another grower's product), where a commingling risk exists even within an all-organic-status framing. |
| `g6_4_handling.commingling_controls_other` | Companion detail field to commingling_controls — same reasoning. |
| `g6_4_handling.handling_records` | §205.103(b) recordkeeping fact. CCOF's G6.4 form does not itemize a records checklist — general recordkeeping obligations are covered by the separate G8.0 Record Keeping form. Trazo asks a handling-specific records checklist here as a superset. |
| `g7_0_labeling.organic_label_categories` | § 205.301 labeling-category tier (100% organic / organic / made with organic). CCOF's G7.0 does not ask which tier an operation sells under as its own question — it only asks about container types, seals, and statements — so this is Trazo capturing an implicit § 205.301 fact the grower form does not itself request. |
| `g7_0_labeling.product_leaves_as_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `product_leaves_as`; not a separate CCOF question — G7.0 A/B ask yes/no per container type, not an open-ended 'other' category. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.additional_records_locations` | Follow-up to `records_location`; see that entry. CCOF has no counterpart question. |

| `g8_0_record_keeping.export_destination_requirements` | Superset — destination-country labeling and production requirements. Not asked by G8.0; CCOF's only export-adjacent line item is the Mexico-import row in A1. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_documentation` | Superset — CCOF's G8.0 A1 table addresses only 'Export from Mexico to the US' (the operation as Exporter of Record); it has no general import-documentation question for an operation importing FROM other countries. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_documentation_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `import_documentation`; not a separate CCOF question. |

| `g8_0_record_keeping.records_access_delegate` | Follow-up to `primary_contact_records_access`; see that entry. CCOF has no counterpart question. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.records_location` | WSDA AGR 2121-O question 5 asks whether all organic records are kept at the primary business location, and routes a No to their AGR 2519. CCOF's G8.0 asks nothing about WHERE records live — its Section A is the record-type table and the five-year retention attestation. Asked of every operation rather than only WSDA's, because § 205.103(c) availability is a fact about the operation, not about the certifier. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.records_maintained_as` | WSDA AGR 2121-O question 7 (electronic / hardcopy). CCOF's G8.0 does not ask what medium the records are kept in. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_name` | Companion detail field to uses_pest_control_company — same reasoning. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_notified` | Companion detail field to uses_pest_control_company — same reasoning (§205.271 notification requirement). |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation_other` | Companion detail field to preventive_measures_documentation, which the Materials Application register (ref F) already cites for the National List material-type table it maps to — this free-text "other" elaboration has no separate CCOF counterpart of its own. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.uses_pest_control_company` | §205.271 requires notifying any contracted pest control operator that the site is certified organic. CCOF's G6.2 form (the only grower form whose B3-B9 substantively maps to G9.0) does not ask whether a contracted pest control company is used as its own distinct checkbox. Trazo asks it directly as a named-company gate. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_detail` | Same reason as fumigant_prohibited_material_used — it is the free-text continuation of that duplicate question, not something NOPB41 asks for. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_used` | NOPB41 (the Grower Materials Application) never asks about fumigant or prohibited-material history — that disclosure belongs to the Parcel Application's land history (NOPB49 §F4/§F8) and the Affidavit of Land History. This restates the same § 205.202(b) fact a second time at the operation level rather than filling a gap CCOF's materials form leaves open. |

### WSDA

| Question | Why it has no WSDA counterpart |
|---|---|
| `w2_0_wild_crop.wild_crop_upload` | WSDA's Wild Harvest section (R) asks only for narrative descriptions of the harvest area, methods, and monitoring — no question requests a site map or landowner statement attachment the way this optional upload offers. |
